title: Evolution's Witness: How Eyes Evolved
author: Ivan R. Schwab
note: Eligible historical and mechanistic explanation of visual systems. Anatomical terminology is demanding and the book has reference uses, but its main narrative explains evolutionary development rather than teaching clinical proficiency or formal methods. The accessible historical explanation provides independent value. No serious veto established; inferred lineages remain less certain than observed anatomy. Ecology is important but optical mechanisms and evolutionary development are central, T11=0; T12=0. Cross-geological account, no single historic endpoint. Mandatory coverage; 19 reader ratings are too small to claim broad reader consensus.
notes: Combines anatomical observations, fossils and genetic evidence; reconstructed evolutionary paths carry greater uncertainty.

title: Gods and Robots: Myths, Machines, and Ancient Dreams of Technology
author: Adrienne Mayor
vetoReason: The recurring interpretation that ancient artificial beings were understood chiefly as manufactured technology rests on contested reconstruction of ancient cognition. Bosak-Schroeder's detailed specialist review challenges this foundation and cites prior scholarship supporting magical interpretations. Mayor's component-based evidence persuades the reviewer in some cases, but does not establish the broader framing. The criticism concerns the central lens, not merely omissions.
note: Not fiction or devotional writing: this is historical analysis of myths and technology. H7 does not exclude the main technology-imagination inquiry. V9 applies despite substantial specialist praise for research and presentation. Considered defense: material components and breakdowns in Talos support some mechanical readings, and Mayor acknowledges opposing views; the reviewer remains unconvinced about broad ancient assumptions. Counterfactual score preserves this foundational uncertainty. Ancient and medieval material dominates; endpoint 1200 yields capped H13. T11=T12=0.
notes: Rich source material, but the central ancient/modern analogy overstates what can be inferred about past beliefs.
Connects myth, craft, technology and cultural imagination; production systems receive little depth.
Some enduring questions of agency and design, with weak transfer from mythical cases.
Interpretation dominates; detailed causal mechanisms of invention are limited.
